content:
Want to use Signal on multiple devices at once? The encrypted messaging service now makes it easier for users to use the app across platforms between iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, rather than being limited to using an iPad as a companion mobile device.

The company also announced support for Android linking today, stating: "We are extending the linked devices feature on iOS, allowing you to link an iPhone to your Signal account, and our support for iPad will continue."

When linking another iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer their complete message history and media files stored in the past 45 days.

Signal said the transfer process uses the same "link-and-sync" technology as that for iPad and desktop devices (including Signal for Mac), with end-to-end encryption used throughout.

This expanded feature is particularly useful for users who need to keep work and personal iPhones separate, and is also suitable for those who need to test multiple devices.

This change also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to the Apple Messages ecosystem, allowing seamless conversations between iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal iOS version 8.22 is now available on the App Store. Signal has previously also launched a username feature, allowing users to contact each other without sharing phone numbers.
